misconceptions.statement: A sprain is an injury to a muscle.
misconceptions.why: Students call every twisted-joint pain a muscle pull.
misconceptions.fix: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament, which joins bone to bone at a joint.

probe.question: Which tissue is hurt in an ankle sprain?
probe.wrong_answer: The muscle

misconceptions.root_belief: similar-sounding words mean the same thing

misconceptions.statement: A strain is an injury to a ligament at a joint.
misconceptions.why: Sprain and strain sound alike and are taught together.
misconceptions.fix: A strain is a stretched or torn muscle or tendon; a tendon joins muscle to bone.

probe.question: A sprinter pulls a hamstring. Is this a sprain or a strain?
probe.wrong_answer: A sprain, because the leg joint is hurt

misconceptions.root_belief: similar-sounding words mean the same thing

misconceptions.statement: If an injured ankle can still bear some weight, it cannot be seriously hurt.
misconceptions.why: Students judge severity only by whether they can still walk.
misconceptions.fix: Some fractures and bad ligament tears still allow weight bearing, so swelling, bruising and tenderness matter too.

probe.question: A player limps on a swollen ankle. Can the injury be ignored since they can walk?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, walking means it is not serious

misconceptions.root_belief: visible function means nothing is wrong
misconceptions.source_hint: clinical guidance on ankle injury assessment (e.g. Ottawa ankle rules literature)

misconceptions.statement: If the joint is only swollen and not bent out of shape, the bone cannot be broken.
misconceptions.why: Films show broken bones as obviously bent.
misconceptions.fix: Some fractures show only swelling, pain and tenderness, so an X-ray by a doctor is needed when unsure.

probe.question: A swollen wrist is not bent. Can the bone be broken?
probe.wrong_answer: No, only a bent wrist means a break

misconceptions.root_belief: serious things always look dramatic

misconceptions.statement: Warming up is a waste of time because muscles are always ready to play.
misconceptions.why: Children play suddenly and feel fine without it.
misconceptions.fix: Light exercise before play raises blood flow and muscle temperature, which lowers the risk of strains.

probe.question: Why do players jog and stretch before a match?
probe.wrong_answer: Just to look professional; it has no effect on injury

misconceptions.root_belief: if I feel fine, no preparation is needed

misconceptions.statement: Resting an injury means staying completely in bed for many days.
misconceptions.why: Rest is imagined as total inactivity.
misconceptions.fix: Rest means avoiding use of the hurt part at first; gentle movement is added back as a doctor or physio advises.

probe.question: After a mild sprain, what does rest mean?
probe.wrong_answer: No movement of any kind for weeks

misconceptions.root_belief: more of a good thing is always better

misconceptions.statement: Ice should be pressed directly on the skin for as long as possible.
misconceptions.why: Students think colder and longer heals faster.
misconceptions.fix: Ice should be wrapped in a cloth and used for about 15 to 20 minutes at a time to avoid frostbite.

probe.question: How should ice be applied to a sprain?
probe.wrong_answer: Directly on skin for an hour

misconceptions.root_belief: bigger or more means more effect

misconceptions.statement: Heat should be applied to a fresh sprain to reduce swelling.
misconceptions.why: Hot water bottles are the usual home remedy for pain.
misconceptions.fix: Heat increases blood flow and can worsen swelling in the first day or two; cold is used first.

probe.question: A fresh ankle sprain is swelling. Hot compress or cold compress?
probe.wrong_answer: Hot compress

misconceptions.root_belief: one remedy works for every kind of pain

misconceptions.statement: The tighter the bandage, the better it works.
misconceptions.why: Students think firm squeezing stops swelling fully.
misconceptions.fix: A compression bandage should be snug but not tight; numbness, tingling or colour change means loosen it.

probe.question: Toes turn blue after bandaging. What should be done?
probe.wrong_answer: Tighten it more

misconceptions.root_belief: bigger or more means more effect

misconceptions.statement: The injured limb should be kept hanging down so blood can reach it.
misconceptions.why: Students think blood must flow to the hurt part to heal it.
misconceptions.fix: Raising the limb above the heart helps fluid drain away and reduces swelling.

probe.question: Where should an injured leg be kept after RICE?
probe.wrong_answer: Hanging down below the body

misconceptions.root_belief: more blood always means more healing

misconceptions.statement: Rubbing and hard massage on a fresh injury makes it heal faster.
misconceptions.why: People instinctively rub a bumped spot and it feels better.
misconceptions.fix: Rubbing a fresh injury can increase bleeding and damage; use RICE and let a doctor decide on massage later.

probe.question: A fresh sprain hurts. Should a friend massage it hard?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, massage speeds up healing

misconceptions.root_belief: what feels soothing must be helping

misconceptions.statement: RICE alone is enough treatment for any sports injury.
misconceptions.why: RICE is taught as the standard first aid.
misconceptions.fix: RICE is first aid for minor injuries; severe pain, deformity, numbness or no improvement needs a doctor.

probe.question: A limb is deformed and very painful. Is RICE enough?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, apply RICE and wait

misconceptions.root_belief: a rule that works sometimes works always

misconceptions.statement: A concussion happens only if the person is knocked unconscious.
misconceptions.why: Films show concussion as a knockout.
misconceptions.fix: Most concussions happen without loss of consciousness; headache, dizziness or confusion are enough to suspect one.

probe.question: A player hit on the head stays awake but is dizzy. Concussion?
probe.wrong_answer: No, they did not faint

misconceptions.root_belief: serious things always look dramatic
misconceptions.source_hint: concussion awareness studies of athletes and coaches

misconceptions.statement: A concussion is only a bruise on the scalp, not a brain injury.
misconceptions.why: Students see only the outside bump.
misconceptions.fix: A concussion is the brain being shaken inside the skull, causing temporary change in brain function, even without any visible mark.

probe.question: No bump is seen after a hit. Can the brain still be injured?
probe.wrong_answer: No, nothing is visible so the brain is fine

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist
misconceptions.source_hint: studies of lay understanding of concussion

misconceptions.statement: Symptoms of concussion always appear immediately after the hit.
misconceptions.why: Injuries like cuts show up at once.
misconceptions.fix: Concussion symptoms can appear minutes to hours or even a day later, so watch the person for 24 to 48 hours.

probe.question: A player seems fine right after a hit. Can they be declared safe forever?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, no symptoms means no concussion

misconceptions.root_belief: effects must appear at once

misconceptions.statement: A helmet makes a player safe from concussion.
misconceptions.why: Helmets are marketed as complete protection.
misconceptions.fix: Helmets prevent skull fractures and cuts well but cannot fully stop the brain from shaking inside the skull.

probe.question: A helmeted cyclist is dazed after a fall. Can they have a concussion?
probe.wrong_answer: No, the helmet protected them

misconceptions.root_belief: a safety device removes all risk
misconceptions.source_hint: sports medicine reviews on helmet effectiveness

misconceptions.statement: You should walk it off or play through pain to show you are tough.
misconceptions.why: Sports culture praises playing through pain.
misconceptions.fix: Pain warns of damage; playing on can turn a small injury into a serious one, so stop and get it checked.

probe.question: A player feels sharp knee pain mid-match. What is best?
probe.wrong_answer: Keep playing and the pain will go away

misconceptions.root_belief: ignoring a warning signal makes the problem go away
misconceptions.source_hint: sports psychology research on playing through pain culture

misconceptions.statement: If the pain disappears after a few minutes, the injury has healed.
misconceptions.why: Students equate no pain with recovery.
misconceptions.fix: Pain can fade while tissue is still damaged, and playing on can re-injure it.

probe.question: Pain stops after 10 minutes of rest. Is the sprain healed?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, no pain means healed

misconceptions.root_belief: no symptom means no problem

misconceptions.statement: A player with a head knock can return in the same match if they say they feel fine.
misconceptions.why: The player's own word seems reliable.
misconceptions.fix: Anyone with suspected concussion must leave play at once and not return that day, as confusion can hide symptoms.

probe.question: A dazed player says they are fine. Back in the game?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they said they are fine

misconceptions.root_belief: the person's own word proves they are fine

misconceptions.statement: After a concussion, a player can resume full sport as soon as the headache goes.
misconceptions.why: Headache is seen as the only sign.
misconceptions.fix: Return must be gradual, step by step, and only after a doctor says it is safe, because the brain needs time to recover.

probe.question: Headache is gone after one day. Full training tomorrow?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the headache is gone

misconceptions.root_belief: one sign tells the whole story
misconceptions.source_hint: return-to-play protocols in sports medicine guidelines

misconceptions.statement: A bandaged or taped joint is as strong as a healthy one, so full play can resume at once.
misconceptions.why: Support products feel secure.
misconceptions.fix: Tape or a brace only supports the joint; the healing ligament still needs rest and rebuilding before full play.

probe.question: A taped ankle feels firm. Can the player sprint hard right away?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the tape makes it as strong as before

misconceptions.root_belief: a safety device removes all risk
